items.title: I’m The Most Transparent, Vilified But I Shall Be Vindicated — Yahaya Bello
items.summary: Former Kogi Governor Yahaya Bello has expressed confidence in his vindication over EFCC allegations of financial misconduct, describing himself as the most transparent yet vilified individual. Bello is facing multiple cases involving alleged misappropriation of ₦110.4 billion and ₦80.2 billion, with charges including criminal breach of trust and money laundering.
items.why: The outcome of Bello's trials will significantly impact perceptions of accountability and anti-corruption efforts in Nigeria's political system.

items.title: Sowore vows to scrap NELFUND, promises N100,000 student grants
items.summary: African Action Congress presidential candidate Omoyele Sowore has promised to replace Nigeria's NELFUND with N100,000 grants per semester for students, arguing that education should not burden graduates with debt. He proposes a four-year student would receive N400,000 total under the scheme.
items.why: This education financing proposal represents a significant policy alternative that could reshape access to higher education and graduate employment prospects in Nigeria.

items.title: Ondo bars underage, unqualified candidates from 2027 WASSCE
items.summary: Ondo State Government has banned underage and unqualified candidates from registering for the 2027 WASSCE through miracle centres to restore educational standards. The policy aims to prevent examination malpractice and ensure credibility of public examinations.
items.why: This measure addresses systemic examination fraud and could set a precedent for maintaining academic integrity across Nigeria's education system.

items.title: 2027: Kaduna APC Deputy Governorship Candidate Woos Women, Lists Uba Sani’s Achievements
items.summary: As political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections gather momentum, the Deputy Governorship Candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Kaduna State, Jerry Adams, has called on women to recognise their critical role in determining the future of the state, insisting that empowering women is central to securing a better society. items.title: NCF urges federations to deploy technology for grassroots development
items.summary: The Nigeria Cricket Federation has urged other sports federations to adopt technology and monitoring systems for grassroots development, using Geographic Information Systems to track coaches and verify participation. NCF targets introducing cricket to 200,000 new participants annually.
items.why: Technology-driven grassroots sports development could serve as a model for expanding athletic participation and talent identification across Nigeria.

items.title: Lagos announces traffic diversion for Saturday’s  Capital City Race
items.summary: Lagos State Government has announced traffic diversions in Ikeja for Saturday's Capital City Race, a 10-kilometre road race expected to attract 3,000 runners. Multiple routes will be affected from 7am with traffic management by various agencies.
items.why: The event demonstrates growing participation in fitness and recreational activities while requiring significant urban traffic coordination.

items.title: 2027: Abiodun says investors bet on Ogun’s political stability, governance continuity
items.summary: Ogun State Governor Dapo Abiodun attributes sustained investor influx to political stability and governance continuity under the APC, citing attraction of over 6,000 companies and construction of 1,700km of roads. He emphasizes the absence of political violence as a major selling point.
items.why: The state's investment success demonstrates how political stability and infrastructure development can drive economic growth and private sector confidence.

items.title: Lagos sets 6,000km fibre goal, 10% startup procurement share
items.summary: Lagos State Government plans to expand its fibre-optic network from 2,400km to 6,000km and allocate 10% of public procurement to startups to boost digital economy growth. The state aims to link research institutions with investors to commercialize innovations.
items.why: The digital infrastructure and procurement initiatives could accelerate Lagos's emergence as a fintech hub and attract private investment.

items.title: Huang: The boy who moved between China and South Africa wants to make Africa’s money move
items.summary: South African fintech Lumepay, co-founded by Harry Huang, has raised $6 million in pre-seed funding to build cross-border payment infrastructure combining banking with stablecoin technology. The platform aims to help African businesses collect, convert and move money across markets.
items.why: Cross-border payment solutions can significantly reduce transaction costs and friction for African businesses engaging in regional and international trade.

items.title: Tinubu appoints new commissioner for National Assembly Service Commission
items.summary: President Tinubu has appointed Agboola Dabiri as Commissioner for the South-West in the National Assembly Service Commission, replacing Taiwo Oluwa who resigned to contest elections. Dabiri previously served as Commissioner for Youth and Social Development in Lagos State.
items.why: The appointment reflects the administration's efforts to maintain institutional continuity and representation in key government bodies ahead of 2027 elections.

items.title: I’ll nominate my son if Obi offers me ministerial job – Babachir Lawal
items.summary: Former Secretary to the Government Babachir Lawal has stated he would nominate his 40-year-old son for ministerial appointment if Peter Obi wins the 2027 presidential election, citing his age and past achievements. Lawal expressed confidence in Obi's electoral victory.
items.why: The statement reflects generational transition discussions within opposition political circles and potential governance structures in a possible Obi administration.

items.title: 22 bag first class degree at TAU
items.summary: Thomas Adewumi University will graduate 111 undergraduates with 22 earning first-class degrees, plus 24 postgraduate students in its 2026 convocation. The university has crossed the symbolic mark of 200 bachelor's degree holders with 70% of undergraduates being women.
items.why: The university's rapid growth and high academic performance demonstrate the emergence of quality private tertiary institutions in Nigeria.

items.title: Lagos governor’s wife seeks deployment of family physicians to 774 LGAs
items.summary: Lagos Governor's wife Dr Ibijoke Sanwo-Olu has called for deployment of family physicians across Nigeria's 774 local government areas to strengthen primary healthcare delivery. She advocates a grassroots approach with physicians strategically positioned to understand community health needs.
items.why: The proposal addresses critical gaps in primary healthcare access and could improve disease prevention and early detection across rural Nigeria.
